text.p: The chairman of Credit Commercial de France (CCF) Charles de Croisset said he expected 1996 to be a good year for the bank.

"Despite a rise in bankruptcies and thanks to a good stock market performance, the year 1996 could be a good year for CCF," De Croisset told a shareholders' meeting in Nice on Monday. His remarks were given in statements released by CCF on Tuesday.

De Croisset told shareholders that all of the group's units look to have emerged from the red this year. "All the group's companies which were experiencing difficulties, abroad or in France, are now profit makers," he said.
De Croisset said CCF's profitability now regularly exceeds the 2.5 percent return generated by the 10-year OAT, and he said CCF hoped to widen the gap further.
He said CCF hoped to raise dividends each year, "results permitting", but that it would consider issuing bonus shares only if it recorded "a very sharp rise in sales and results".
CCF reported first-half net attributable profit of 668.8 million francs, up 12.2 percent over the same period for 1995.
